question: Your data contains a reaction time in milliseconds and an accuracy score between 0 and 1. What happens if you run a PCA without standardizing the features first?

answers.answer: PC1 points almost exactly along the reaction time
answers.feedback: Correct! Reaction times in milliseconds have a much larger variance than a score between 0 and 1, so they dominate the direction of maximal variance.

answers.answer: PC1 points almost exactly along the accuracy score
answers.feedback: Not quite. PCA looks for the largest variance. Which feature varies more in absolute numbers?

answers.answer: Nothing, PCA does not depend on the units of the features
answers.feedback: Not quite. The variance of a feature depends on its units, and PCA is based on the variance.

question: A dataset has 200 observations and 10 variables. How many principal components can PCA find at most?

answers.feedback: Correct! With p variables, there are at most p components (as long as there are more observations than variables).
Not quite. The components are directions in the space of the variables. How many dimensions does this space have?
Not quite. Each component is a new axis in the space of the variables.

question: What is the main difference between PCR and PLS?

answers.answer: PLS uses the target y to build its components, PCR does not
answers.feedback: Correct! PCR uses the principal components of X, which are found without looking at y. PLS looks for directions that covary with y.

answers.answer: PCR is a regression method, PLS is a classification method
answers.feedback: Not quite. Both are regression methods.

answers.answer: PLS always predicts better than PCR
answers.feedback: Not quite. PLS can find predictive directions that PCR misses, but it can also adapt more to the training data. In practice, both often perform similarly.

question: You fit a PCR model with all p components. Which model do you get?

answers.answer: The same model as ordinary linear regression with all predictors
answers.feedback: Correct! The p components contain exactly the same information as the p predictors, so nothing is reduced.

answers.answer: A model with less variance than linear regression
answers.feedback: Not quite. Only keeping fewer components reduces the variance.
Not quite. PCR does not shrink the coefficients.

question: After PCR with 3 components, can you tell which of the original predictors are irrelevant for the model?

answers.answer: No, each component is a weighted sum of all predictors
answers.feedback: Correct! All predictors still enter the model through the components. If you want to remove predictors, use Lasso or subset selection.

answers.answer: Yes, the predictors that are not part of the 3 components are irrelevant
answers.feedback: Not quite. Every predictor contributes to every component, even if some loadings are small.
